[Director 指令] [Patch] 新实验结果批量更新，影响 Table 1 + Discussion + Claim 3。

## 1. LLaMA CoNLL 结果（exp_017_llama_conll_infer）— 强 model-agnostic 证据

LLaMA-3.1-8B CoNLL NER (N=8, T=1.0):
- SJ rho=0.431, FK rho=0.428, logprob rho=0.307
- greedy_f1=0.927, oracle_f1=0.944, headroom=0.018
- structural_beats_surface=true

与 Qwen CoNLL 对比：SJ rho 几乎一致（0.431 vs 0.436, Δ=0.005）。**这是最强的 model-agnostic 证据**。

**写作注意**：
- CoNLL oracle headroom 仅 0.018（LLaMA）/ 0.032（Qwen）。不能 claim "consistency enables meaningful quality improvement on CoNLL"——聚焦 correlation/discrimination (rho, AUROC)
- SJ vs FK advantage 在 CoNLL 上仅 0.004（vs SciERC 上 +0.10~0.16）。Discussion 需讨论：CoNLL 标注清晰、实体类型少（4 类），SJ soft matching 优势不显著。SJ 的优势在 schema 复杂度高的数据集（SciERC 6 类）上更明显

## 2. WNUT-17 负面结果（D045）— Claim 3 支撑

WNUT-17 NER (Qwen, N=16, T=1.0): SJ rho=0.062 (p=0.106 不显著), 54% F1=0, logprob rho=-0.411。
- 论文中作为 Claim 3 capability boundary 的跨域证据
- 与 RE 的 44% F1=0 模式一致：模型能力不足时所有信号失效
- logprob 强负相关值得在 Discussion 讨论（可能的 calibration 问题）

## 3. 3-seed NER 汇总（D046）

SciERC NER (Qwen, N=16): seed42=0.428, seed123=0.424, seed456=0.384。
- Mean ρ=0.412±0.025, 全部 structural>surface
- 论文报告 mean±std

## 4. 跨配置全景表（可作 Table 或 Supplementary）

| 配置 | SJ rho | structural>surface? |
|------|--------|---------------------|
| SciERC NER, Qwen, N=16, 3-seed | 0.412±0.025 | ✅ |
| CoNLL NER, Qwen, N=8 | 0.436 | ✅ |
| CoNLL NER, LLaMA, N=8 | 0.431 | ✅ |
| SciERC NER, LLaMA, N=8 | 0.363 | ✅ |
| SciERC RE (all) | 0.21-0.30 | ❌ voting_conf 更优 |
| WNUT-17 NER | 0.062 | ❌ 模型能力不足 |

NER 4/4 配置 pass。RE 和 WNUT-17 是诚实讨论的局限。

这次不用验证引用。

ML research experiment management tools

attachment.content:
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review changed code for reuse, quality, and efficiency, then fix any issues found.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled remote agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring remote agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Build, debug, and optimize Claude API / Anthropic SDK apps. Apps built with this skill should include prompt caching. Also handles migrating existing Claude API code between Claude model versions (4.5 → 4.6, 4.6 → 4.7, retired-model replacements).
TRIGGER when: code imports `anthropic`/`@anthropic-ai/sdk`; user asks for the Claude API, Anthropic SDK, or Managed Agents; user adds/modifies/tunes a Claude feature (caching, thinking, compaction, tool use, batch, files, citations, memory) or model (Opus/Sonnet/Haiku) in a file; questions about prompt caching / cache hit rate in an Anthropic SDK project.
SKIP: file imports `openai`/other-provider SDK, filename like `*-openai.py`/`*-generic.py`, provider-neutral code, general programming/ML.
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a pull request
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

          venue: "TACL 2025"
        - key: "cocoa_vashurin_2025"
          title: "CoCoA: Combining Confidence and Consistency for LLM Uncertainty Quantification"
          venue: "NeurIPS 2025"
          arxiv: "2502.04964"
          differentiation: "MBR framework fusing confidence+consistency. Parallels our exp-016 ensemble (SJ+logprob) but not structured IE."
        - key: "vashurin_uq_eval_2025"
          title: "Systematic Evaluation of UQ Methods for LLMs"
          arxiv: "2510.20460"
          differentiation: "VCE/MSP/SC/CoCoA four-method evaluation. Tasks exclude structured IE — our work fills this gap."
    verification_status: "pending — Director says need WebSearch verification for bib accuracy"
    dependencies: [introduction]

  - section: method
    word_budget: 1000
    core_bullets:
      - "Problem formulation: given LLM M, input x, N stochastic samples {y_1,...,y_N}, define confidence signal c(x, {y_i}) → ℝ"
      - "Signal 1 — Log-probability: c_lp(y_i) = (1/|y_i|) Σ log p(t_j|t_{<j}, x). Per-sample signal. Clarify: sequence-level mean, not token-level max."
      - "Signal 2 — Exact-match voting: c_em(x) = max_y |{i: y_i = y}| / N. Instance-level."
      - "Signal 3 — Fleiss' Kappa (FK): token-level inter-rater agreement. Instance-level."
      - "Signal 4 — Soft Jaccard (SJ): set-aware structural similarity via type-grouped bipartite matching. Instance-level. Key: uses Hungarian matching with max(|A|,|B|) normalization."
      - "Signal 5 — Entity voting confidence: per-entity majority voting rate, averaged. Instance-level."
      - "Distinction: log-prob is PER-SAMPLE (ranks candidates), others are INSTANCE-LEVEL (aggregate across samples). This distinction is central to the correlation-selection gap."
      - "Evaluation: quality estimation (ρ, τ, AUROC vs F1) and sample selection (best-of-N F1)"
    dependencies: []
    notation_table:
      M: "language model"
      x: "input instance"
      y_i: "i-th stochastic sample"
      N: "number of samples"
      c: "confidence signal"
      SJ: "soft Jaccard similarity"
      FK: "Fleiss' Kappa"
      EM: "exact-match voting rate"

  - section: experiments
    word_budget: 2400
    subsections:
      - name: setup
        word_budget: 500
        core_bullets:
          - "Datasets: SciERC (science, 551 test, NER+RE joint), CoNLL-2003 (news, 3453 test, NER), WNUT-17 (social media, NER — method boundary analysis)"
          - "Model: Qwen3-8B fine-tuned with LoRA (r=32) per dataset. LLaMA-3.1-8B-Instruct for cross-model validation (exp_007)."
          - "Sampling: N=8 primary, N=16 for scaling analysis. T=1.0 standard, T=0.7 for robustness."
          - "Evaluation: greedy F1 as reference, per-instance F1 vs each signal's ρ/τ/AUROC, best-of-N selection F1"
          - "Implementation: vLLM inference, XGrammar constrained decoding, span realignment post-processing"

      - name: quality_estimation
        word_budget: 600
        core_bullets:
          - "Table 1: All 5 signals × {SciERC NER, SciERC RE, CoNLL NER} × {ρ, τ, AUROC}"
          - "SciERC NER (exp_015 unified): voting 0.728 > SJ 0.666 >> FK 0.624 ≈ EM 0.623 >> logprob 0.559 (AUROC). ρ: voting 0.502 >> SJ 0.357 > FK 0.265 ≈ EM 0.257 >> logprob 0.140"
          - "CoNLL NER: EM 0.816 > SJ 0.801 > EV 0.789 > FK 0.774 > logprob 0.753 — EM > SJ on easy task!"
          - "SciERC RE (exp_015 unified): voting 0.716 > logprob 0.635 ≈ FK 0.631 > SJ 0.582 > EM 0.504 — degraded (AUROC). ρ: voting 0.422 > FK 0.253 ≈ logprob 0.247 > SJ 0.211 > EM 0.100"
          - "Key: voting is NER strongest single signal (ρ=0.502); within consistency family voting >> SJ per-instance but SJ offers unique cross-condition robustness (temp Δρ numerically small: NER 0.014, RE 0.010; cond ρ=0.412). EM dominates on easy tasks (CoNLL). D035: FORBIDDEN 'SJ ≈ voting'."
        registry_refs: [mvp_pilot_004, exp_012_logprob_baseline, exp_013_exact_match_voting, exp_014_entity_majority_voting, exp_015_metrics_expansion, exp_002]
        tables: [tab_quality_estimation]

      - name: correlation_selection_gap
        word_budget: 600
        core_bullets:
          - "Table 2: Best-of-N selection F1 for each signal vs greedy vs oracle"
          - "NER: greedy 0.609 ≥ ALL signals (logprob 0.609, SJ 0.604, voting 0.596). Oracle 0.769 (+16pp headroom)"
          - "RE: logprob 0.397 > greedy 0.374 (+2.4pp). SJ 0.368, voting 0.338 ≈ random. Oracle 0.561 (+18.7pp)"
          - "CoNLL: voting 0.914 > greedy 0.912 (+0.18pp) — first instance where voting beats greedy, on easy task"
          - "Explanation: instance-level signals predict WHICH INPUTS are reliable, not WHICH OUTPUTS are best. Only per-sample logprob can rank candidates."
          - "Ensemble analysis: SJ+voting NER ρ=0.489 (+23%), AUROC 0.735 (+3.5pp). But ensemble SELECTION still fails."
        registry_refs: [exp_016_signal_ensemble, exp_002]
        tables: [tab_selection]
        figures: [fig_selection_gap]

      - name: task_complexity
        word_budget: 400
        core_bullets:
          - "Signal ranking shifts with task difficulty: CoNLL (easy, F1=0.91) EM>SJ; SciERC NER (hard, F1=0.66) SJ>EM; SciERC RE (harder) all signals converge to ~0.28 ρ — compound error ceiling. Unified framework: structural signals strongest within model capability range; beyond it all signals converge."
          - "RE diagnostic: FEATURE-OF near-zero ρ, HYPONYM-OF ρ=0.65. Entity span errors = 55.5% of RE FN."
          - "Fisher z-test: NER ρ_sj significantly > RE ρ_sj (p=0.021)"
          - "Compound error propagation: head_sj ρ=0.21 (vs NER 0.38) — fundamental, not formula issue"
          - "exp_009 capability stratification (Claim 3): SJ strength scales with entity count — 6+ entities ρ=0.547, 1-2 entities ρ=0.415. SJ >> logprob advantage stable across all sentence length quartiles (Δρ≈0.08-0.20). Three independent proxies (F1, sent_len, ent_count) weakly correlated (|r|<0.15), confirming robustness is not confounded."
        registry_refs: [exp_004_re_diagnostic, e1_component_wise_re_sj, exp_002, exp_009_capability_stratification]

      - name: analysis
        word_budget: 300
        core_bullets:
          - "Temperature robustness: SJ numerically small sensitivity — NER Δρ=0.014 (moderate), RE Δρ=0.010 (robust); FK NER Δρ=0.06, RE Δρ=0.097 (high sensitivity). Bootstrap 95% CI all include 0 → differences not statistically significant → use 'numerically small' not 'significantly'. D038: logprob excluded from T comparison (no T=0.7 logprob data). Conditional filtering >> temperature tuning scope does NOT include logprob."
          - "N-scaling: NER SJ improves N=8→16 (ρ 0.357→0.428, +0.071), FK only +0.016 — SJ scaling gain 4.4× FK. Cross-seed Δ<0.01 (0.428/0.424). RE N=16: logprob ρ=0.287 > SJ 0.281 ≈ FK 0.279 (all flat, compound error ceiling)."
          - "LOO-SJ: Δρ=-0.014, evaluation circularity minimal"
          - "Conditional filtering: NER cond SJ ρ=0.412, RE cond SJ ρ=0.368 (N=8) / 0.308 (N=16) vs logprob cond ρ=-0.026 (N=16, completely fails). Separating knowledge-gap errors critical — structural signals retain value, logprob collapses."
          - "Cross-model: LLaMA-3.1-8B confirms SJ>FK on NER (ρ 0.363 vs 0.327), RE cond SJ recovers (0.405 vs 0.259). Pattern model-agnostic."
        registry_refs: [exp_005, exp_001_ner_n16_scierc, exp_001_seed42_v2, exp_001_seed123_v2, exp_008_re_n16_v2, exp_015_metrics_expansion, exp_007_llama_inference]
        figures: [fig_signal_heatmap]

      - name: method_boundary
        word_budget: 400
        core_bullets:
          - "D029: WNUT-17 as method boundary analysis — When Does Structural Consistency Fail?"
          - "WNUT-17 SJ ρ=0.082 near-zero. Root cause: training data 63.8% empty instances (vs SciERC 0%), model learns strong empty-output prior"
          - "16/16 samples all empty → SJ=1.0 but F1=0, systematically inflates consistency for wrong predictions"
          - "Logprob also fails: empty predictions get logprob=-0.007 (extreme high confidence), ρ=-0.41 (anti-correlated)"
          - "Conditional filtering partially helps: post-filter logprob ρ=+0.35, but SJ remains weak"
          - "Conclusion: SJ effectiveness requires model to have basic task competence — degenerate training data (>50% empty) invalidates all unsupervised signals"
          - "This is NOT a dataset limitation but a method boundary: identifies preconditions for structural consistency"
        registry_refs: [exp_003_wnut17_eval]

    registry_refs: [mvp_pilot_004, mvp_pilot_005, exp_001_ner_n16_scierc, exp_001_seed42_v2, exp_001_seed123_v2, exp_008_re_n16_v2, exp_002, exp_004_re_diagnostic, exp_005, exp_012_logprob_baseline, exp_013_exact_match_voting, exp_014_entity_majority_voting, exp_015_metrics_expansion, exp_016_signal_ensemble, e1_component_wise_re_sj, exp_007_llama_inference, exp_003_wnut17_eval, exp_009_capability_stratification]
    tables: [tab_quality_estimation, tab_selection]
    figures: [fig_selection_gap, fig_signal_heatmap, fig_reliability]

  - section: discussion
    word_budget: 500
    core_bullets:
      - "When WOULD consistency help: (a) poor calibration (ICL without fine-tuning), (b) closed-source APIs (no logprob), (c) ensemble/mixture settings, (d) systematically overconfident models"
      - "Non-obviousness of negative result: self-consistency works for reasoning (+18pp GSM8K), structured prediction has rich internal structure, the DEGREE of gap and task-complexity boundary are not predictable a priori"
      - "Practical recommendations: quality estimation → voting (strongest per-instance) or SJ (when temperature-robustness/generalizability matters); best-of-N → logprob (RE only); NER → greedy is near-optimal"
      - "SJ unique positioning: same consistency family as voting but complementary — (a) temperature numerically stable (NER Δρ=0.014, RE Δρ=0.010; bootstrap CI includes 0), (b) generalizes to any structured output not limited to entity, (c) conditional filtering ρ=0.412 still strong, (d) with voting ensemble AUROC 0.735. Framing: 'voting stronger per-instance, SJ more robust cross-condition'. D038: FORBIDDEN 'significantly' for temperature — use 'numerically small'."
      - "Conditional analysis as unique contribution: separating knowledge-gap errors (RE ~44% zero-F1, WNUT-17 ~64% empty) reveals hidden signal value — SJ recovers on RE cond (ρ=0.308 at N=16) while logprob collapses (ρ=-0.026)"
      - "Capability boundary framework: structural signals are strongest quality estimators within model capability range; beyond it (RE compound errors), all signals converge — but conditional filtering restores structural advantage"
      - "Limitations: 1 RE dataset (SciERC, 44% zero-F1 limits signal discrimination), 2 model families (Qwen3 + LLaMA), no supervised upper bound beyond logistic regression proxy. RE zero-F1 proportion must be explicitly noted."
    dependencies: [experiments]

  - section: conclusion
    word_budget: 300
    core_bullets:
      - "Summary: first systematic comparison of confidence signals for quality estimation vs selection in generative IE"
      - "Three findings: (1) structural consistency best for quality estimation, (2) correlation-selection gap, (3) task-complexity boundary"
      - "Future work: supervised verifiers, cross-task transfer of confidence signals, conformal prediction integration, scaling to larger models"
    dependencies: [experiments, discussion]

visualization_plan:
  - fig_id: fig_overview
    type: conceptual
    tool: matplotlib
    description: >
      Overview figure (1-column) illustrating the paper's core finding. Left: quality estimation
      (consistency signals predict which instances are reliable). Right: sample selection (the same
      signals fail to pick the best sample). Shows the conceptual distinction between instance-level
      and per-sample signals. Simple schematic with boxes and arrows — not a full architecture diagram.
    placement: introduction
    aspect_ratio: "2:1"
    data_source: "manual"

  - fig_id: fig_selection_gap
    type: statistical
    tool: matplotlib
    description: >
      Two-panel figure. Left panel: grouped bar chart of AUROC for quality estimation (5 signals,
      SciERC NER). Right panel: grouped bar chart of best-of-N selection F1 (same 5 signals + greedy
      + oracle, SciERC NER + RE). Horizontal dashed line at greedy F1. Visualizes the gap: high AUROC
      does NOT translate to high selection F1. Include error bars from bootstrap CI where available.
    data_source: "registry: exp_016_signal_ensemble, exp_012_logprob_baseline, exp_014_entity_majority_voting"
    placement: experiments
    aspect_ratio: "2:1"

  - fig_id: fig_signal_heatmap
    type: statistical
    tool: matplotlib
    description: >
      Heatmap (signals as rows, datasets/tasks as columns) showing Spearman ρ values. Columns:
      SciERC NER (N=8), SciERC RE (N=8), CoNLL NER (N=8). Rows: voting_conf, SJ, EM, FK, logprob.
      Color-coded from red (low) to green (high). Annotated with ρ values. Visualizes task-complexity
      boundary: signal ranking shifts across columns.
    data_source: "registry: exp_015_metrics_expansion (SciERC NER+RE unified), exp_002 (CoNLL). D035: heatmap data source unified to exp_015."
    placement: experiments
    aspect_ratio: "4:3"

  - fig_id: fig_reliability
    type: statistical
    tool: matplotlib
    description: >
      Reliability diagram (2 panels: NER, RE). For each signal, bin instances by predicted confidence
      (decile), plot mean predicted confidence vs mean actual F1. Perfect calibration = diagonal.
      Shows which signals are well-calibrated vs overconfident. Focus on SJ, voting_conf, logprob (3 curves per panel).
    caption_notes: >
      Caption or surrounding text MUST note two definition differences:
      (1) F1 definition: y-axis uses mean_sample_f1 (average F1 across N stochastic samples per instance),
      distinct from greedy F1 used in Table 1 ρ/AUROC targets — this is the calibration-appropriate measure
      since confidence signals aggregate over stochastic samples.
      (2) Logprob normalization: logprob is globally min-max normalized to [0,1] (SJ and voting_conf are
      naturally [0,1]). ECE absolute values are therefore NOT directly comparable across signals — only
      relative calibration patterns (over/under-confident regions) are meaningful.
    data_source: "registry: mvp_pilot_004, exp_012_logprob_baseline, exp_014_entity_majority_voting"
    placement: experiments
    aspect_ratio: "2:1"

Pivot from \\\"TTS improvement\\\" to \\\"confidence estimation + correlation-selection gap\\\".\\n\\n## Target Venue\\n- Primary: EMNLP 2026 Main (via ARR May 2026)\\n- Fallback: EMNLP 2026 Findings\\n- Deadline: ARR May cycle, 2026-05-25\\n\\n## Core Claims (3 条)\\n\\n### Claim 1 (Positive — Quality Estimation)\\nStructural consistency signals (entity voting confidence, soft Jaccard) are the strongest unsupervised quality estimators for entity-level IE, significantly outperforming model confidence (log-probability) and surface agreement (FK, exact-match) at instance-level quality prediction. Entity voting achieves AUROC 0.73 / ρ=0.50 on NER, SJ achieves AUROC 0.67 / ρ=0.36 — both far above logprob (AUROC 0.56 / ρ=0.14). ### Claim 1 (Positive — Quality Estimation)
Structural consistency signals (entity voting confidence, soft Jaccard) are the strongest unsupervised quality estimators for entity-level IE, significantly outperforming model confidence (log-probability) and surface agreement (FK, exact-match) at instance-level quality prediction. ### Claim 2 (Novel Finding — Correlation-Selection Gap)
Instance-level quality estimation ≠ per-sample selection ability. Despite strong instance-level correlation (ρ≈0.39-0.43), NO unsupervised confidence signal beats greedy decoding for NER best-of-N selection. ### Claim 3 (Diagnostic — task-complexity boundary)
The effectiveness of consistency-based confidence is governed by task structural complexity: compound error propagation in relational tasks degrades the consistency-accuracy correlation on the full instance set, but the signal remains valid within the model's capability range. This boundary applies across all confidence signals tested.

- **Mitigation**: exp-012 (log-prob), exp-013 (exact-match), exp-014 (entity voting) provide comprehensive baseline comparison. Results: structural consistency family (SJ+voting) >> log-prob >> FK ≈ exact-match. USC discussed in related work (LLM-as-judge, orthogonal approach).
- **Priority**: P0, RESOLVED — results decisive

### R3b: "Voting confidence beats SJ — why use SJ?"
- **Mitigation**: SJ generalizes to arbitrary structured outputs (relations, events, any set-structured prediction). Voting is entity-specific. NER full: voting leads (ρ=0.50 vs 0.36), but SJ retains unique strength in conditional evaluation (ρ=0.41 vs voting 0.45) and is more temperature-robust (Δρ=±0.01). RE cond: SJ ρ=0.37 competitive with voting 0.46. SJ is also more interpretable (pairwise similarity). Paper presents both as complementary instantiations of the structural consistency principle, with voting as practical default and SJ as robust/generalizable option.
- **Priority**: P1 — narrative adjustment needed given exp_015 unified values

### R4: "No actual TTS improvement demonstrated"
- **Status**: ⚠️ CONFIRMED NEGATIVE by exp-016. Best-of-N selection DOES NOT beat greedy on NER with any signal. RE: only logprob +2.4pp over greedy.
- **Mitigation**: Paper PIVOTS to "confidence estimation + correlation-selection gap analysis." exp-006 redesigned as diagnostic: show selection curves to visualize the gap (F1 vs N per signal + oracle ceiling). The gap itself is a contribution, not a failure.
- **Priority**: P0 — narrative pivot required

### R5: "Sample size N=8 may be too small for reliable SJ estimation"
- **Mitigation**: exp-001 (N=16) with multi-seed robustness
- **Priority**: P0

### R6: "Conditional analysis cherry-picks favorable instances"
- **Mitigation**: Principled separation (knowledge-gap vs uncertainty). Add threshold sensitivity analysis. Temperature analysis provides independent validation.
- **Priority**: P0 (add sensitivity analysis)

### R7: "Only ρ as evaluation metric"
- **Mitigation**: Add AUROC, calibration plots, Kendall's τ for all experiments
- **Priority**: P0

### R8: "Formula-implementation discrepancy"
- **Mitigation**: Paper must describe actual algorithm (type-grouped Hungarian matching with max(|g_a|,|g_b|) denominator)
- **Priority**: P0, paper writing fix

### R9: "Evaluation circularity (T>0 consistency vs T=0 F1)"
- **Mitigation**: Add leave-one-out SJ evaluation as robustness check. Justify cross-mode design (greedy = deterministic reference, standard in TTS literature).
- **Priority**: P0

### R10: "Insufficient related work" (三档一致 [B][M][W])
- **Mitigation**: Expand to 35+ references. Must cite:
  - USC (Chen 2024) — empirical differentiation, not just citation
  - Semantic uncertainty (Kuhn 2023), calibration (Kadavath 2022, Guo 2017, Desai & Durrett 2020)
  - **Conformal prediction for structured outputs**: Fisch et al. 2021, Angelopoulos et al. 2021, Bates et al. 2021
  - **Token-level NER uncertainty**: Xiao & Wang 2019, Shelmanov et al. 2021, He et al. 2020
  - **Ensemble/MC-dropout**: Lakshminarayanan et al. 2017, Gal & Ghahramani 2016
  - **Verifier/reward models**: Cobbe et al. 2021, Lightman et al. 2023
  - **TTS scaling theory**: Snell et al. 2024, Brown et al. 2024
  - **Structured calibration**: Kuleshov & Liang 2015, Jagannatha & Yu 2022
  - **IE confidence**: Culotta & McCallum 2004
  - SelfCheckGPT (Manakul 2023), selective prediction (Geifman & El-Yaniv 2017)
  - **[2025-2026 新颖性自查补充 — 必引]**:
    - CISC (ACL Findings 2025) — confidence-weighted majority vote for reasoning; 对比：我们用 structural similarity 而非 confidence 加权，且面向 set-structured IE 输出
    - Self-Certainty Best-of-N (ICLR 2026, arxiv 2502.18581) — KL-divergence reward-free selection; 对比：我们发现 log-prob 是唯一有效 selection signal (与其方向互补)，且揭示 correlation-selection gap
    - ReASC (2026, arxiv 2601.02970) — reliability-aware adaptive self-consistency; 对比：仍限于 reasoning 离散答案
    - Atomic Self-Consistency (EMNLP 2024) — 子声明级一致性 for long-form text; 对比：我们在 entity-set 级别做结构化度量
    - **Nédellec & Xia (Genomics Informatics, 2026-02, PMC12888769)** — "Consistency–accuracy correlation in hard-prompted LLMs for entity and relation extraction"。最直接竞争者：4 LLMs 在植物健康 NER/RE 上研究 consistency-accuracy 相关性。**关键差异**：(a) 他们用 surface-level string matching，自承"overlooks semantically consistent outputs"，我们的 SJ 正好解决此问题; (b) 不研究 best-of-N selection; (c) 单领域 hard-prompted (T=0); (d) 无多信号家族对比。论文 Intro 可引用其 limitation 作为 SJ 的动机
  - **[2025-2026 新颖性自查补充 — 应引]**:
    - UQ for LLMs Survey (ACL Findings 2025) — 最全面 LLM 不确定性综述
    - UQ+Calibration Survey (arxiv 2503.15850, 2025) — 第二篇综合综述
    - Semantic Entropy Probes (2024) — 低成本不确定性估计
    - Latent Self-Consistency (2025, arxiv 2508.18395) — embedding 空间一致性
    - Ranked Voting SC (2025, arxiv 2505.10772) — 排名投票变体，仍限于推理任务
    - Know Your Limits: Abstention Survey (TACL 2025) — 选择性预测综述，与 Claim 1 selective prediction 角度直接相关
    - Confidence Estimation Survey (NAACL 2024, arxiv 2311.08298) — LLM 置信度估计全景定位
    - **CoCoA (Vashurin et al., NeurIPS 2025, arxiv 2502.04964)** — MBR 框架融合 confidence+consistency 做 UQ，在 QA/摘要/翻译上评估。与我们 exp-016 ensemble (SJ+logprob) 对标，但未涉及 structured IE
    - **Vashurin et al. (arxiv 2510.20460, 2025)** — VCE/MSP/Sample Consistency/CoCoA 四方法系统评估，任务不含 structured IE
  - **需新增 Related Work 小节**:
    - "Test-Time Scaling & Sample Selection" — 将 CISC/Self-Certainty/ReASC 集中讨论，明确 positioning：现有工作均面向 reasoning/QA 的离散答案，我们首次在 structured IE 上做系统信号对比并发现 correlation-selection gap
    - "Consistency for Structured IE" — 引 Nédellec & Xia 2026 作为同期工作，显式对比：surface matching vs structural metrics (SJ)；他们的 limitation 是我们的 motivation
- **Priority**: P0, Paper Agent handles

### R11: "SJ+logprob ensemble missing" (Dream 2 — both reviewers)
- **Status**: ✅ RESOLVED by exp-016. Results:
  - Ensemble AUROC: NER 0.735 (+3.5pp over best single), RE 0.719 (−0.2pp, no improvement)
  - Linear combo: SJ+voting best at α=0.3 (NER ρ=0.489); RE α=0.0 (pure voting)
  - FK negative coefficient in logistic regression → surface agreement is net-negative when structural signals present
  - **Interpretation**: voting_conf captures nearly all discriminative information; ensemble adds marginal value on NER, none on RE. Supports the "structural consistency family" narrative.
- **Priority**: DONE — write into paper with honest interpretation

### R12: "No supervised upper bound / reward model comparison" (Dream 2)
- **Mitigation**: Simple logistic regression on [SJ, FK, logprob, voting_conf, EM] as proxy for trained verifier (included in exp-016). Full reward model training out of scope for this paper — discuss as future work.
- **Priority**: P1 (partially addressed by exp-016 ensemble)

### R13: "Headroom capture rate low (37% NER, 11% RE)" (Dream 2)
- **Mitigation**: Discuss explicitly in paper. Contextualize vs other unsupervised TTS methods. Argue that the information-theoretic ceiling for unsupervised signals is unknown — our result establishes a baseline.
- **Priority**: P0, paper writing

### R14: "Cross-model validation thin — need more than 2×8B" (Dream 2)
- **Mitigation**: exp-017 (LLaMA on CoNLL, P1). 70B model infeasible within GPU budget. Acknowledge as limitation.
- **Priority**: P1

### R15: "Log-prob definition ambiguity — Eq.1 vs best-of-N ranking" (Dream 2 cross-tier, [W])
- **Mitigation**: Paper must clarify: log-prob ranks among N candidates (each sample's generation log-prob), not just score greedy output. Cost comparison table must state "all best-of-N require N forward passes; log-prob adds zero ranking overhead."
- **Priority**: P0, Paper Agent handles

### R16: "Zero figures — data-rich paper with only tables" (Dream 2 cross-tier, [W])
- **Mitigation**: Paper Agent must include ≥3 figures: (1) selection curves (F1 vs N for each signal + oracle), (2) reliability diagram (calibration), (3) N-scaling or cost-effectiveness scatter. Data exists from exp-010/015.
- **Priority**: P0, Paper Agent handles

### R17: "Diagnostic framework overclaimed — descriptive not prescriptive" (Dream 2 cross-tier, [M][W])
- **Mitigation**: Soften "diagnostic framework" to "diagnostic analysis" throughout. Current taxonomy (ceiling/floor/compound error) is descriptive. Either formalize with a priori metrics or reframe as empirical analysis.
- **Priority**: P0, Paper Agent handles

### R18: "No discussion of when consistency WOULD help" (Dream 2 cross-tier, [W])
- **Mitigation**: Add discussion paragraph: consistency should outperform log-prob when (a) model calibration is poor (in-context learning without fine-tuning), (b) log-prob unavailable (closed-source APIs), (c) ensemble/mixture settings, (d) tasks where model is systematically overconfident.
- **Priority**: P1, Paper Agent handles

### R19: "Negative result partially predictable for fine-tuned models" (Dream 2 cross-tier, [W])
- **Mitigation**: Paper must argue non-obviousness: (a) self-consistency demonstrably helps for reasoning tasks (Wang et al. 2023), (b) structured prediction has internal structure that surface metrics can't capture, (c) the DEGREE of log-prob's strength and the task-complexity boundary are not predictable a priori.
- **Priority**: P1, Paper Agent handles

## Venue Fit

EMNLP is well-suited for:
- Systematic empirical comparison of confidence signals for structured prediction
- Diagnostic findings with principled explanations
- The "comparison + boundary condition" contribution pattern

Risk assessment (post-Dream 2, all tiers 3/6):
- **Structural risks (三档一致)**: (1) novelty perceived as incremental, (2) related work thin, (3) single RE dataset. These are presentation/positioning issues, NOT data issues — fixable by Paper Agent.
- **Data-dependent risks (观察中)**: SJ vs LOGPROB ranking may be dataset-dependent (Dream imagined this; awaiting exp-002/003 real data). If confirmed → reframe as "complementary signals" rather than "SJ dominates."
- **Confirmed strength**: SJ >> LOGPROB on SciERC (AUROC 0.70 vs 0.59). Structural consistency family consistently top on existing data.
- **Critical path**: Paper Agent (related work 35+ refs, 3+ figures, contribution reframe) > new GPU experiments.

core_bullets:
          - "Table 1: All 5 signals × {SciERC NER, SciERC RE, CoNLL NER} × {ρ, τ, AUROC}"
          - "SciERC NER (exp_015 unified): voting 0.728 > SJ 0.666 >> FK 0.624 ≈ EM 0.623 >> logprob 0.559 (AUROC). ρ: voting 0.502 >> SJ 0.357 > FK 0.265 ≈ EM 0.257 >> logprob 0.140"
          - "CoNLL NER: EM 0.816 > SJ 0.801 > EV 0.789 > FK 0.774 > logprob 0.753 — EM > SJ on easy task!"
          - "SciERC RE (exp_015 unified): voting 0.716 > logprob 0.635 ≈ FK 0.631 > SJ 0.582 > EM 0.504 — degraded (AUROC). ρ: voting 0.422 > FK 0.253 ≈ logprob 0.247 > SJ 0.211 > EM 0.100"
          - "Key: voting is NER strongest single signal (ρ=0.502); within consistency family voting >> SJ per-instance but SJ offers unique cross-condition robustness (temp Δρ numerically small: NER 0.014, RE 0.010; cond ρ=0.412). EM dominates on easy tasks (CoNLL). D035: FORBIDDEN 'SJ ≈ voting'."
        registry_refs: [mvp_pilot_004, exp_012_logprob_baseline, exp_013_exact_match_voting, exp_014_entity_majority_voting, exp_015_metrics_expansion, exp_002]
        tables: [tab_quality_estimation]

      - name: correlation_selection_gap
        word_budget: 600
        core_bullets:
          - "Table 2: Best-of-N selection F1 for each signal vs greedy vs oracle"
          - "NER: greedy 0.609 ≥ ALL signals (logprob 0.609, SJ 0.604, voting 0.596). Oracle 0.769 (+16pp headroom)"
          - "RE: logprob 0.397 > greedy 0.374 (+2.4pp). SJ 0.368, voting 0.338 ≈ random. Oracle 0.561 (+18.7pp)"
          - "CoNLL: voting 0.914 > greedy 0.912 (+0.18pp) — first instance where voting beats greedy, on easy task"
          - "Explanation: instance-level signals predict WHICH INPUTS are reliable, not WHICH OUTPUTS are best. Only per-sample logprob can rank candidates."
          - "Ensemble analysis: SJ+voting NER ρ=0.489 (+23%), AUROC 0.735 (+3.5pp). But ensemble SELECTION still fails."
        registry_refs: [exp_016_signal_ensemble, exp_002]
        tables: [tab_selection]
        figures: [fig_selection_gap]

      - name: task_complexity
        word_budget: 400
        core_bullets:
          - "Signal ranking shifts with task difficulty: CoNLL (easy, F1=0.91) EM>SJ; SciERC NER (hard, F1=0.66) SJ>EM; SciERC RE (harder) all signals converge to ~0.28 ρ — compound error ceiling. Unified framework: structural signals strongest within model capability range; beyond it all signals converge."
          - "RE diagnostic: FEATURE-OF near-zero ρ, HYPONYM-OF ρ=0.65. Entity span errors = 55.5% of RE FN."
          - "Fisher z-test: NER ρ_sj significantly > RE ρ_sj (p=0.021)"
          - "Compound error propagation: head_sj ρ=0.21 (vs NER 0.38) — fundamental, not formula issue"
          - "exp_009 capability stratification (Claim 3): SJ strength scales with entity count — 6+ entities ρ=0.547, 1-2 entities ρ=0.415. SJ >> logprob advantage stable across all sentence length quartiles (Δρ≈0.08-0.20). Three independent proxies (F1, sent_len, ent_count) weakly correlated (|r|<0.15), confirming robustness is not confounded."
        registry_refs: [exp_004_re_diagnostic, e1_component_wise_re_sj, exp_002, exp_009_capability_stratification]

      - name: analysis
        word_budget: 300
        core_bullets:
          - "Temperature robustness: SJ numerically small sensitivity — NER Δρ=0.014 (moderate), RE Δρ=0.010 (robust); FK NER Δρ=0.06, RE Δρ=0.097 (high sensitivity). Bootstrap 95% CI all include 0 → differences not statistically significant → use 'numerically small' not 'significantly'. D038: logprob excluded from T comparison (no T=0.7 logprob data). Conditional filtering >> temperature tuning scope does NOT include logprob."
          - "N-scaling: NER SJ improves N=8→16 (ρ 0.357→0.428, +0.071), FK only +0.016 — SJ scaling gain 4.4× FK. Cross-seed Δ<0.01 (0.428/0.424). RE N=16: logprob ρ=0.287 > SJ 0.281 ≈ FK 0.279 (all flat, compound error ceiling)."
          - "LOO-SJ: Δρ=-0.014, evaluation circularity minimal"
          - "Conditional filtering: NER cond SJ ρ=0.412, RE cond SJ ρ=0.368 (N=8) / 0.308 (N=16) vs logprob cond ρ=-0.026 (N=16, completely fails). Separating knowledge-gap errors critical — structural signals retain value, logprob collapses."
          - "Cross-model: LLaMA-3.1-8B confirms SJ>FK on NER (ρ 0.363 vs 0.327), RE cond SJ recovers (0.405 vs 0.259). Pattern model-agnostic."
        registry_refs: [exp_005, exp_001_ner_n16_scierc, exp_001_seed42_v2, exp_001_seed123_v2, exp_008_re_n16_v2, exp_015_metrics_expansion, exp_007_llama_inference]
        figures: [fig_signal_heatmap]

      - name: method_boundary
        word_budget: 400
        core_bullets:
          - "D029: WNUT-17 as method boundary analysis — When Does Structural Consistency Fail?"
          - "WNUT-17 SJ ρ=0.082 near-zero. Root cause: training data 63.8% empty instances (vs SciERC 0%), model learns strong empty-output prior"
          - "16/16 samples all empty → SJ=1.0 but F1=0, systematically inflates consistency for wrong predictions"
          - "Logprob also fails: empty predictions get logprob=-0.007 (extreme high confidence), ρ=-0.41 (anti-correlated)"
          - "Conditional filtering partially helps: post-filter logprob ρ=+0.35, but SJ remains weak"
          - "Conclusion: SJ effectiveness requires model to have basic task competence — degenerate training data (>50% empty) invalidates all unsupervised signals"
          - "This is NOT a dataset limitation but a method boundary: identifies preconditions for structural consistency"
        registry_refs: [exp_003_wnut17_eval]
